brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Level 0 and level 1 stacked over cell (0,0): piece:0,0,0 full base and piece:0,0,1 full base, with a snap joint between them and a 2-compartment bin (bin:0,0,1~hex-bin-full-div2) in the upper storey.

Compact footprint of about 3 cells on level 0 (full bases at (-1,0), (0,0), half base at (1,0)). The configurator does not check fit against a specific bench; I did not measure the bench, and I did not add any mounting to it.
Two notch drawer frames (notch:0#0,1#notch1 and notch:0#-1,1#notch1, hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm) fill the empty level-0 positions (0,1) and (-1,1), each between two touching bases.

finish.summary: Built a two-storey hex storage tower: full bases stacked at (0,0) for levels 0 and 1, a half base at (1,0) and a full base at (-1,0) on level 0, two notch drawer frames on the front of level 0, and a 2-compartment bin in the upper storey. Open faces are capped and joints locked; check_build reports no issues and meshClash is clear. I did not add props. The bench fit is not verified.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
